````markdown
# M9 — Loop Prompts

_Live end-to-end Kaggle regression test on
[Spaceship Titanic](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/spaceship-titanic/overview)._
_For sequential, partly autonomous execution on Arch Linux._
_Prerequisite: M8.5 exit confirmed (CI green + GitHub Issues/PR/labels interface in place; see `docs/m8_5-final-review.md`)._
_Shared rules: every Loop Prompt below MUST follow `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` (sequencing, no real Kaggle/Anthropic outside designated approval paths, DB DSN + sandbox bypass, worktree commit/push/PR at milestone end, secret denylist)._

---

## M9 at a glance

M9 is the **first end-to-end live Kaggle regression** for this platform. It
exercises the M3 worker, M5 research path, M6 reviewer + telemetry, the M7
permission policy, and the M8 decision_api + UI shell against a real Kaggle
competition. The competition is Spaceship Titanic — binary classification,
public leaderboard, no cash prize, safe for repeated dry-run iteration and a
single real submission under an explicit human-approval gate.

M9 is **not** a leaderboard-chasing milestone. The acceptance criterion is
that the loop *runs end-to-end correctly under the approval gates*, not that
the LB score is high. The CV thresholds in `docs/milestones.md` §M9 are
sanity guards, not targets.

Direct entry into M9 is blocked until **all** are true:

- M8.5-T001 (CI repair) is merged on main.
- M8.5-T002 (engineering practice + GitHub interface) is merged on main and
  `.github/labels.yml` has been synced to `origin` (33 labels visible via
  `gh label list`).
- `scripts/sync_labels.py --dry-run` reports `0 update`.
- `docs/m8_5-final-review.md` exists and reports PASS.

### What's in scope

| Capability | Owned by | M9 touches |
|---|---|---|
| Kaggle credentials handling | `env.example`, `.env`, `KAGGLE_USERNAME`/`KAGGLE_KEY` | T000 — verifies env without printing secrets; gates submit on presence |
| Competition register + workspace | `tools/kca/competition.py` (`register`, `clone`, `list`, `info`) | T000 / T001 |
| Data download + checksum | `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_download`, `cmd_verify` (sha256 manifest already implemented in M5) | T001 |
| Worker loop (research → baseline → CV → submission file) | `src/worker/` + `tools/kca/run.py` + skills | T002 |
| Reviewer gate before submit | `src/worker/reviewer.py` + `services/decision_api/` + UI Approval Inbox | T003 |
| Real Kaggle submit (under approval) | `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_submit` + `kaggle competitions submit` | T004 — single real call |
| Second experiment (HGB / feature engineering) | same worker, second run | T005 |
| Regression assertions | `tests/test_m9_e2e.py` + `runs` table | T006 / T007 |
| GitHub issue / label workflow | `.github/labels.yml`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`, `.github/pull_request_template.md`, `policy:approval-required` | every task — work order issue per task |
| Final review | `milestone-final-review` skill + `worktree-milestone-pr` skill | T008 |

### What's NOT in scope

- Running Kaggle submit / kernel push / dataset upload / model upload outside
  T004's single approved call.
- Changing production Supabase.
- Implementing M9 follow-ups from M8 (multi-user auth, artifact preview via
  signed URLs, live-DB CI on fork PRs, OTEL collector wiring). Those are
  separate milestones; if M9 surfaces blockers for them, file follow-up
  issues — don't expand scope.
- Adding new CLI subcommands. M9 uses the existing `kca` surface
  (`competition`, `kaggle`, `run`, `research`, `review`, `decisions`,
  `skill`) without inventing new ones.
- Runtime submission-format detection. KCA's `kca kaggle submit` is
  format-agnostic: it passes `--file` straight to `kaggle competitions
  submit`, and Kaggle validates server-side. **M9 assumes
  `submission.csv` because Spaceship Titanic is a CSV competition.** Other
  competition shapes (code-competition notebooks → `kca kaggle push`;
  `submission.zip`; JSON; etc.) need different paths that KCA does not
  yet auto-select. Tracked as a separate `area:kaggle` / `type:feature`
  follow-up — see M9-T002's "Submission-format note" for context.

DB / sandbox details: see `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §3 — the local
`supabase-db` container (`postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`)
needs `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`.

---

|---|---|---|
| M9-T000 | Kaggle credentials + competition registration (no real submit, no secret print) | Prompt 0 |
| M9-T001 | Download Spaceship Titanic data, verify sha256 manifest, commit `manifest.json` | Prompt 1 |

| M9-T006 | Regression assertions: CV ≥ 0.78 (LR), ≥ 0.80 (HGB); LB recorded | Prompt 6 |
| M9-T007 | `tests/test_m9_e2e.py` (dry-run path, no credentials) | Prompt 7 |

## GitHub issue / label workflow for M9

Each M9 task is filed as a GitHub issue using the `feature-work.yml` form,
labelled per task type:

| Task | Issue labels at file time | Labels added by triage | Labels at merge |
|---|---|---|---|
| M9-T000 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:kaggle`, `area:config`, `area:security` | `ai:ready` (after AC + owner) | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M9-T001 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M9-T002 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M9-T003 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:supabase`, `area:ui` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M9-T004 | `type:feature`, `ai:blocked`, `policy:approval-required`, `decision:needed`, `area:kaggle`, `priority:P0` | `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready` only after human comment "approved to submit" | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M9-T005 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M9-T006 | `type:test-gap`, `ai:triage`, `area:testing` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M9-T007 | `type:test-gap`, `ai:triage`, `area:testing`, `area:ci` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M9-T008 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:release`, `area:docs` | `ai:ready` after T000–T007 closed | `ai:implementing` → close |

T004 is the only task that starts `ai:blocked` and requires a
`decision:confirmed` comment with an explicit "approved to submit" record
before triage may promote it to `ai:ready`. This is enforced by the
`github-issue-triage` agent rules in `.claude/skills/github-issue-triage/`.

The PR for each task uses `.github/pull_request_template.md`. The
"Remote side effects" section is load-bearing: T004's PR is the ONLY
M9 PR that may check the "Live Kaggle call" box, and must link the
approval comment from the closing issue.

---

## Approval gates (summary)

| Gate | When it fires | Where the approval is recorded | Who can approve |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kaggle_submit` | Worker stages a submission file and calls into `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_submit` | `human_decisions` row + comment on the closing GitHub issue | Project owner / reviewer named on the issue |
| `kernel_push` | Not used in M9 | n/a (out of scope) | n/a |
| `dataset_upload` | Not used in M9 | n/a (out of scope) | n/a |
| `model_upload` | Not used in M9 | n/a (out of scope) | n/a |

The Kaggle approval flow inside M9 is:

```
worker stages submission.csv
  → reviewer-gate writes agent_reviews row + agent_job_events
  → decision_api surfaces pending decision (POST /decisions queued)
  → UI Approval Inbox renders pending decision
  → human approves via UI (POST /decisions/<id>/approve) OR
    `kca decisions approve --id <id>`
  → human comments "approved to submit" on the closing issue
  → triage agent promotes issue to `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready`
  → M9-T004 Loop Prompt runs ONE `kca kaggle submit`
  → LB score recorded; submissions row written
  → PR opens with the approval comment linked
```

A second real Kaggle submission inside M9 is **out of scope**. If a
follow-up experiment in M9-T005 turns out to need its own LB score,
file it as a new M10+ issue and gate it the same way.

## Rollback / stop criteria

Stop the milestone — do **not** advance to the next Loop Prompt — if any of
these is true:

- A real Kaggle submit returns an error from Kaggle (rate limit, bad CSV,
  rules violation). The fix path is local: regenerate the submission and
  re-request approval; do NOT silently retry.
- The reviewer gate (M9-T003) fails to fire when it should, or fires
  when it shouldn't.
- Any `policy:approval-required` issue advances without the corresponding
  `decision:confirmed` label and comment.
- Any test in the validation suite regresses from green to red.
- The DSN, credentials, or `.env*` are accidentally printed in any log,
  audit row, or PR. Stop and rotate the credential immediately.
- CV scores diverge from the M9-T006 thresholds in a way that suggests a
  leakage bug (e.g. CV near 1.0). Investigate before submitting.

If M9 needs a new architectural decision (e.g. multi-user auth, a new
queue, or a new artifact storage shape), **pause and ask** — those are
M10+ decisions, not M9 expansion. Open an ADR draft in `docs/adr/` and
stop the milestone there.
````

```python
REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7–9. Worker tool_call paths
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _build_test_worker(tmp_path, monkeypatch, decision):
    """Shared setup helper for the three worker_tool_call tests."""
    import types as _types

    from src.worker._types import JobPolicy
    from src.worker.worker import AgentWorker, MockLiteLLMClient

    monkeypatch.setenv("KCA_AUDIT_PATH", str(tmp_path / "audit.jsonl"))
    (tmp_path / "hello.txt").write_text("hi")

    policy = JobPolicy(
        skill_name="_test_fixture",
        policy_profile="permissive-dev",
        mode="default",
        tool_decisions={"read_file": decision},
    )
    worker = AgentWorker(
        job_id="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
        prompt="read it",
        policy=policy,
        workspace=tmp_path,
        db_url=None,
        dry_run=True,
    )

    client = MockLiteLLMClient(scenario="two_turns")
    state = {"n": 0}

    def completion(**_kwargs):
        state["n"] += 1
        if state["n"] == 1:
            tc = _types.SimpleNamespace(
                id="c",
                type="function",
                function=_types.SimpleNamespace(
                    name="read_file",
                    arguments=json.dumps({"path": "hello.txt"}),
                ),
            )
            msg = _types.SimpleNamespace(content=None, tool_calls=[tc])
            return _types.SimpleNamespace(
                choices=[
                    _types.SimpleNamespace(message=msg, finish_reason="tool_calls")
                ],
                usage=_types.SimpleNamespace(prompt_tokens=10, completion_tokens=5),
            )
        msg = _types.SimpleNamespace(content="done", tool_calls=None)
        return _types.SimpleNamespace(
            choices=[_types.SimpleNamespace(message=msg, finish_reason="stop")],
            usage=_types.SimpleNamespace(prompt_tokens=5, completion_tokens=2),
        )

    client.completion = completion  # type: ignore[method-assign]
    worker._mock_client = client
    return worker


def _read_audit(tmp_path):
    p = tmp_path / "audit.jsonl"
    if not p.is_file():
        return []
    return [json.loads(line) for line in p.read_text().splitlines() if line]


def test_worker_tool_call_allow_path(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    worker = _build_test_worker(tmp_path, monkeypatch, "allow")
    result = worker.run()
    assert result.status == "done"
    rows = _read_audit(tmp_path)
    assert any(r["tool_name"] == "read_file" and r["decision"] == "allow" for r in rows)


def test_worker_tool_call_ask_path(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    worker = _build_test_worker(tmp_path, monkeypatch, "ask")
    result = worker.run()
    assert result.status == "paused"
    rows = _read_audit(tmp_path)
    assert any(r["decision"] == "ask" for r in rows)


def test_worker_tool_call_deny_path(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    worker = _build_test_worker(tmp_path, monkeypatch, "deny")
    result = worker.run()
    assert result.status == "failed"
    assert result.stop_reason == "policy_violation"
    rows = _read_audit(tmp_path)
    assert any(r["decision"] == "deny" for r in rows)
```

```python
"""kca DB access layer (psycopg3, sync).

Side-effect classification:
  - Operations against a local Supabase stack are LOCAL_WRITE.
  - Operations against a remote Postgres are REMOTE_WRITE and require
    both KCA_DB_TARGET=remote and KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1.

Env contract (set in .env, loaded automatically via python-dotenv if installed):
  - SUPABASE_DB_URL         : libpq conninfo string (preferred).
  - KCA_DB_TARGET           : "local" (default) or "remote".
  - KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE        : "1" to allow remote/submission operations.
  - SUPABASE_DB_HOST/PORT/USER/PASSWORD/DB : fallback discrete vars.

Module is importable without a live DB — connections happen lazily.
```

```python
"""M9 smoke tests — regression assertions for Spaceship Titanic.

This module is **assertion-only**. It does not retrain models, does not
re-submit to Kaggle, and does not write to the DB. It reads the metrics
recorded by:

  - M9-T002 (baseline LR, ``experiment_runs.external_run_id='baseline-lr'``)
  - M9-T005 (HGB + feature engineering, ``external_run_id='hgb-fe-v1'``)
  - M9-T004 (the single approved real Kaggle submission, recorded in
    ``submissions.public_score``; the submissions row's
    ``experiment_run_id`` FK points back to the baseline-lr run)

and asserts:

  - ``cv_lr >= 0.78``         (M9 sanity guard, see docs/milestones.md §M9)
  - ``cv_hgb >= 0.80``        (M9 sanity guard)
  - ``cv_hgb > cv_lr``        (HGB beat LR on the same CV split)
  - ``public_score IS NOT NULL`` for the M9-T004 submission row

Tests are DB-aware and SKIP cleanly when ``SUPABASE_DB_URL`` is unset, so
the no-DB CI job stays green. The live-DB CI job runs them.

Run with:
    python -m pytest tests/test_m9_smoke.py -v
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT / "tools" / "kca"))

requires_db = pytest.mark.skipif(
    not os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_URL"),
    reason="SUPABASE_DB_URL not set",
)

# M9 thresholds — these are sanity guards copied from docs/milestones.md §M9.
# They are deliberately well below the recorded values so a real regression
# (data leakage, broken CV split, mis-recorded metric) trips them, but
# routine variance from seed/version drift does not.
LR_CV_FLOOR = 0.78
HGB_CV_FLOOR = 0.80

# External run names (experiment_runs.external_run_id).
LR_RUN_NAME = "baseline-lr"
HGB_RUN_NAME = "hgb-fe-v1"

# The one real Kaggle submission from M9-T004, identified by its
# Kaggle-side submission id. Looking up by external_submission_id keeps
# the test stable across DB recreations.
M9_T004_EXTERNAL_SUBMISSION_ID = "52955657"


def _fetch_cv_accuracy(cur, external_run_id: str) -> float:
    """Return the recorded cv_accuracy for an experiment_runs row.

    Reads ``metrics->'cv_accuracy'->>'value'`` which is the shape
    written by the M2 metrics path (see ``tools/kca/db.py::record_metric``).
    """
    cur.execute(
        """
        SELECT (metrics->'cv_accuracy'->>'value')::float AS cv_accuracy
        FROM experiment_runs
        WHERE external_run_id = %s
        ORDER BY created_at DESC
        LIMIT 1
        """,
        (external_run_id,),
    )
    row = cur.fetchone()
    assert row is not None, f"no experiment_runs row with external_run_id={external_run_id!r}"
    cv = row[0]
    assert cv is not None, (
        f"experiment_runs[{external_run_id!r}].metrics->'cv_accuracy'->>'value' is NULL"
    )
    return float(cv)


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def m9_metrics():
    """Read all four M9 regression metrics from the DB in one connection."""
    import psycopg

    with psycopg.connect(os.environ["SUPABASE_DB_URL"]) as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cv_lr = _fetch_cv_accuracy(cur, LR_RUN_NAME)
            cv_hgb = _fetch_cv_accuracy(cur, HGB_RUN_NAME)

            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT id, public_score, experiment_run_id
                FROM submissions
                WHERE external_submission_id = %s
                """,
                (M9_T004_EXTERNAL_SUBMISSION_ID,),
            )
            sub = cur.fetchone()

    assert sub is not None, (
        f"no submissions row with external_submission_id={M9_T004_EXTERNAL_SUBMISSION_ID!r}; "
        "M9-T004 LB record is missing"
    )
    return {
        "cv_lr": cv_lr,
        "cv_hgb": cv_hgb,
        "submission_id": sub[0],
        "public_score": sub[1],
        "submission_experiment_run_id": sub[2],
    }


@requires_db
def test_lr_cv_meets_floor(m9_metrics):
    cv = m9_metrics["cv_lr"]
    assert cv >= LR_CV_FLOOR, (
        f"LR baseline cv_accuracy={cv:.6f} fell below M9 floor {LR_CV_FLOOR}; "
        "do NOT lower the threshold — investigate the run first"
    )


@requires_db
def test_hgb_cv_meets_floor(m9_metrics):
    cv = m9_metrics["cv_hgb"]
    assert cv >= HGB_CV_FLOOR, (
        f"HGB+FE cv_accuracy={cv:.6f} fell below M9 floor {HGB_CV_FLOOR}; "
        "do NOT lower the threshold — investigate the run first"
    )


@requires_db
def test_hgb_beats_lr_on_cv(m9_metrics):
    cv_lr = m9_metrics["cv_lr"]
    cv_hgb = m9_metrics["cv_hgb"]
    assert cv_hgb > cv_lr, (
        f"HGB CV {cv_hgb:.6f} did NOT beat LR CV {cv_lr:.6f}; "
        "the second experiment is expected to improve over the baseline"
    )


@requires_db
def test_m9_t004_public_score_recorded(m9_metrics):
    score = m9_metrics["public_score"]
    assert score is not None, (
        f"submissions row for external_submission_id="
        f"{M9_T004_EXTERNAL_SUBMISSION_ID!r} has NULL public_score"
    )
    # Sanity: a Kaggle accuracy LB score sits in (0, 1].
    assert 0.0 < float(score) <= 1.0, (
        f"public_score={score!r} outside plausible range (0, 1]"
    )

```

````markdown
# Milestone Loop Protocol

_Shared rules that apply to every milestone Loop Prompt (M0+) unless a
milestone explicitly overrides one._

Each `docs/m*-loop-prompts.md` should reference this file once at the top
rather than duplicating the rules per prompt.

---

## 1. Sequencing

- Loop Prompts within a milestone MUST execute in order.
- Each prompt's **acceptance checks MUST pass** before moving to the next.
- On failure: fix the specific issue and **retry that prompt only**; do
  not skip ahead and do not redo prompts that already passed.

## 2. External systems and side effects

- Do NOT call the **real Anthropic API or Kaggle API** outside of paths
  the milestone explicitly designates as live; default to `--dry-run`.
- Do NOT run real **Kaggle submit / kernel push / dataset upload /
  model upload** unless the milestone explicitly requests it AND a
  human-approval record exists.
- Do NOT change **production Supabase**.

## 3. Database validation

- Use `SUPABASE_DB_URL=postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`
  — the `supabase-db` container on the local Docker network.
- Container IPs change on `docker compose down/up`; refresh with:
  ```bash
  docker inspect supabase-db \
    --format '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}'
  ```
- DB calls and LAN-host calls require `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`.
  Cloud LLM calls stay **inside** the sandbox.

## 4. Reporting

- Report **PASS / FAIL / SKIP** inline for each prompt's verification
  step.
- At milestone end, write the milestone's defined **Closeout format**
  (see each milestone's last Loop Prompt for the exact fields).

## 5. Git / GitHub — worktree mode

This project executes each milestone inside a dedicated **git worktree**
branched off `main`.

- **Mid-milestone, mid-prompt:** do not `git commit` or `git push`
  unless the individual task spec explicitly says so. Stage with
  `git add` and surface diffs in the inline report.
- **At milestone end** — once every Loop Prompt has PASSed and the
  milestone's Closeout has been written — Claude Code SHOULD:
  1. `git add` only the files listed in the Closeout's "files changed"
     section (or its equivalent).
  2. `git commit` using either:
     - one squash commit per milestone, OR
     - one commit per Loop Prompt,
     depending on the milestone's preference. The default is **one
     commit per Loop Prompt**, with the milestone's final review as the
     last commit.
  3. `git push` the worktree's branch to the remote.
  4. `gh pr create` against `main` using the milestone's
     `docs/m{N}-final-review.md` as the PR body.

- The following **still require explicit human approval** at any time:
  - `git push --force` (any branch)
  - `gh pr merge` (any PR)
  - any push to `main` directly
  - any `gh label create/edit/delete`, `gh issue edit/comment`,
    `gh pr edit/comment` against issues or PRs **not** owned by this
    milestone

- If the milestone's task spec or scope says
  "do not commit / push / open PRs", that override **wins** — typically
  used for planning-only or evidence-only milestones.

## 6. Secrets and forbidden reads

These are always denied, regardless of milestone:

- `.env*`
- `**/kaggle.json`, `~/.kaggle/kaggle.json`
- `~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, any private key contents
- `~/.aws/**`, `~/.config/gcloud/**`
- `secrets/**`

Shell commands that would surface the above (`cat`, `grep`, `head`,
`tail`, `less`, `more`, file uploads) over these paths are blocked at
the hook layer.

---

## How a milestone references this file

In each Loop Prompt block, instead of repeating the rules above, include
one line near the top:

```
Follow: docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md
```

A milestone's `docs/m{N}-loop-prompts.md` should still spell out:

- the milestone's own scope, non-goals, and task list;
- per-Loop-Prompt read lists, scope, acceptance criteria;
- any **override** of a default in this file (e.g. a planning-only
  milestone overriding the worktree commit/push behavior).

````

````markdown
# M9 — Loop Prompts

_Live end-to-end Kaggle regression test on
[Spaceship Titanic](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/spaceship-titanic/overview)._
_For sequential, partly autonomous execution on Arch Linux._
_Prerequisite: M8.5 exit confirmed (CI green + GitHub Issues/PR/labels interface in place; see `docs/m8_5-final-review.md`)._
_Shared rules: every Loop Prompt below MUST follow `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` (sequencing, no real Kaggle/Anthropic outside designated approval paths, DB DSN + sandbox bypass, worktree commit/push/PR at milestone end, secret denylist)._

---

## M9 at a glance

M9 is the **first end-to-end live Kaggle regression** for this platform. It
exercises the M3 worker, M5 research path, M6 reviewer + telemetry, the M7
permission policy, and the M8 decision_api + UI shell against a real Kaggle
competition. The competition is Spaceship Titanic — binary classification,
public leaderboard, no cash prize, safe for repeated dry-run iteration and a
single real submission under an explicit human-approval gate.

M9 is **not** a leaderboard-chasing milestone. The acceptance criterion is
that the loop *runs end-to-end correctly under the approval gates*, not that
the LB score is high. The CV thresholds in `docs/milestones.md` §M9 are
sanity guards, not targets.

Direct entry into M9 is blocked until **all** are true:

- M8.5-T001 (CI repair) is merged on main.
- M8.5-T002 (engineering practice + GitHub interface) is merged on main and
  `.github/labels.yml` has been synced to `origin` (33 labels visible via
  `gh label list`).
- `scripts/sync_labels.py --dry-run` reports `0 update`.
- `docs/m8_5-final-review.md` exists and reports PASS.

### What's in scope

| Capability | Owned by | M9 touches |
|---|---|---|
| Kaggle credentials handling | `env.example`, `.env`, `KAGGLE_USERNAME`/`KAGGLE_KEY` | T000 — verifies env without printing secrets; gates submit on presence |
| Competition register + workspace | `tools/kca/competition.py` (`register`, `clone`, `list`, `info`) | T000 / T001 |
| Data download + checksum | `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_download`, `cmd_verify` (sha256 manifest already implemented in M5) | T001 |
| Worker loop (research → baseline → CV → submission file) | `src/worker/` + `tools/kca/run.py` + skills | T002 |
| Reviewer gate before submit | `src/worker/reviewer.py` + `services/decision_api/` + UI Approval Inbox | T003 |
| Real Kaggle submit (under approval) | `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_submit` + `kaggle competitions submit` | T004 — single real call |
| Second experiment (HGB / feature engineering) | same worker, second run | T005 |
| Regression assertions | `tests/test_m9_e2e.py` + `runs` table | T006 / T007 |
| GitHub issue / label workflow | `.github/labels.yml`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`, `.github/pull_request_template.md`, `policy:approval-required` | every task — work order issue per task |
| Final review | `milestone-final-review` skill + `worktree-milestone-pr` skill | T008 |

### What's NOT in scope

- Running Kaggle submit / kernel push / dataset upload / model upload outside
  T004's single approved call.
- Changing production Supabase.
- Implementing M9 follow-ups from M8 (multi-user auth, artifact preview via
  signed URLs, live-DB CI on fork PRs, OTEL collector wiring). Those are
  separate milestones; if M9 surfaces blockers for them, file follow-up
  issues — don't expand scope.
- Adding new CLI subcommands. M9 uses the existing `kca` surface
  (`competition`, `kaggle`, `run`, `research`, `review`, `decisions`,
  `skill`) without inventing new ones.
- Runtime submission-format detection. KCA's `kca kaggle submit` is
  format-agnostic: it passes `--file` straight to `kaggle competitions
  submit`, and Kaggle validates server-side. **M9 assumes
  `submission.csv` because Spaceship Titanic is a CSV competition.** Other
  competition shapes (code-competition notebooks → `kca kaggle push`;
  `submission.zip`; JSON; etc.) need different paths that KCA does not
  yet auto-select. Tracked as a separate `area:kaggle` / `type:feature`
  follow-up — see M9-T002's "Submission-format note" for context.

DB / sandbox details: see `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §3 — the local
`supabase-db` container (`postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`)
needs `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`.

## GitHub issue / label workflow for M9

Each M9 task is filed as a GitHub issue using the `feature-work.yml` form,
labelled per task type:

| Task | Issue labels at file time | Labels added by triage | Labels at merge |
|---|---|---|---|
| M9-T000 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:kaggle`, `area:config`, `area:security` | `ai:ready` (after AC + owner) | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M9-T001 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M9-T002 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M9-T003 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:supabase`, `area:ui` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M9-T004 | `type:feature`, `ai:blocked`, `policy:approval-required`, `decision:needed`, `area:kaggle`, `priority:P0` | `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready` only after human comment "approved to submit" | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M9-T005 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M9-T006 | `type:test-gap`, `ai:triage`, `area:testing` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M9-T007 | `type:test-gap`, `ai:triage`, `area:testing`, `area:ci` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M9-T008 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:release`, `area:docs` | `ai:ready` after T000–T007 closed | `ai:implementing` → close |

T004 is the only task that starts `ai:blocked` and requires a
`decision:confirmed` comment with an explicit "approved to submit" record
before triage may promote it to `ai:ready`. This is enforced by the
`github-issue-triage` agent rules in `.claude/skills/github-issue-triage/`.

The PR for each task uses `.github/pull_request_template.md`. The
"Remote side effects" section is load-bearing: T004's PR is the ONLY
M9 PR that may check the "Live Kaggle call" box, and must link the
approval comment from the closing issue.

---

## Approval gates (summary)

| Gate | When it fires | Where the approval is recorded | Who can approve |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kaggle_submit` | Worker stages a submission file and calls into `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_submit` | `human_decisions` row + comment on the closing GitHub issue | Project owner / reviewer named on the issue |
| `kernel_push` | Not used in M9 | n/a (out of scope) | n/a |
| `dataset_upload` | Not used in M9 | n/a (out of scope) | n/a |
| `model_upload` | Not used in M9 | n/a (out of scope) | n/a |

The Kaggle approval flow inside M9 is:

```
worker stages submission.csv
  → reviewer-gate writes agent_reviews row + agent_job_events
  → decision_api surfaces pending decision (POST /decisions queued)
  → UI Approval Inbox renders pending decision
  → human approves via UI (POST /decisions/<id>/approve) OR
    `kca decisions approve --id <id>`
  → human comments "approved to submit" on the closing issue
  → triage agent promotes issue to `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready`
  → M9-T004 Loop Prompt runs ONE `kca kaggle submit`
  → LB score recorded; submissions row written
  → PR opens with the approval comment linked
```

A second real Kaggle submission inside M9 is **out of scope**. If a
follow-up experiment in M9-T005 turns out to need its own LB score,
file it as a new M10+ issue and gate it the same way.

---

## Rollback / stop criteria

Stop the milestone — do **not** advance to the next Loop Prompt — if any of
these is true:

- A real Kaggle submit returns an error from Kaggle (rate limit, bad CSV,
  rules violation). The fix path is local: regenerate the submission and
  re-request approval; do NOT silently retry.
- The reviewer gate (M9-T003) fails to fire when it should, or fires
  when it shouldn't.
- Any `policy:approval-required` issue advances without the corresponding
  `decision:confirmed` label and comment.
- Any test in the validation suite regresses from green to red.
- The DSN, credentials, or `.env*` are accidentally printed in any log,
  audit row, or PR. Stop and rotate the credential immediately.
- CV scores diverge from the M9-T006 thresholds in a way that suggests a
  leakage bug (e.g. CV near 1.0). Investigate before submitting.

If M9 needs a new architectural decision (e.g. multi-user auth, a new
queue, or a new artifact storage shape), **pause and ask** — those are
M10+ decisions, not M9 expansion. Open an ADR draft in `docs/adr/` and
stop the milestone there.
````

```python
def _build_test_worker(tmp_path, monkeypatch, decision):
    """Shared setup helper for the three worker_tool_call tests."""
    import types as _types

    from src.worker._types import JobPolicy
    from src.worker.worker import AgentWorker, MockLiteLLMClient

    monkeypatch.setenv("KCA_AUDIT_PATH", str(tmp_path / "audit.jsonl"))

    policy = JobPolicy(
        skill_name="_test_fixture",
        policy_profile="permissive-dev",
        mode="default",

    )
    worker = AgentWorker(
        job_id="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
        prompt="read it",
        policy=policy,
        workspace=tmp_path,
        db_url=None,
        dry_run=True,
    )

    client = MockLiteLLMClient(scenario="two_turns")
    state = {"n": 0}

    def completion(**_kwargs):
        state["n"] += 1
        if state["n"] == 1:
            tc = _types.SimpleNamespace(
                id="c",
                type="function",
                function=_types.SimpleNamespace(
                    name="read_file",
                    arguments=json.dumps({"path": "hello.txt"}),
                ),
            )
            msg = _types.SimpleNamespace(content=None, tool_calls=[tc])
            return _types.SimpleNamespace(

                usage=_types.SimpleNamespace(prompt_tokens=10, completion_tokens=5),

        return _types.SimpleNamespace(

            usage=_types.SimpleNamespace(prompt_tokens=5, completion_tokens=2),

    client.completion = completion  # type: ignore[method-assign]

def _read_audit(tmp_path):
    p = tmp_path / "audit.jsonl"
    if not p.is_file():

    return [json.loads(line) for line in p.read_text().splitlines() if line]
```

```python
"""M8 worker-wiring tests — JobPolicy.tool_decisions + ToolSpec enforcement.

Three approval paths: allow / ask / deny. Each runs the worker against a
mocked LiteLLM client so no real network or model calls happen, and asserts
the matching audit JSONL line plus the worker's stop_reason.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
import types
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))

from src.worker._types import JobPolicy  # noqa: E402
from src.worker.worker import AgentWorker, MockLiteLLMClient  # noqa: E402


def _single_call_client(tool_name: str, tool_input: dict) -> MockLiteLLMClient:
    """LiteLLM mock that emits one tool call then stops."""

    client = MockLiteLLMClient(scenario="two_turns")
    turn = {"n": 0}

    def completion(**_kwargs):
        turn["n"] += 1
        if turn["n"] == 1:
            tc = types.SimpleNamespace(
                id="call_x",
                type="function",
                function=types.SimpleNamespace(
                    name=tool_name,
                    arguments=json.dumps(tool_input),
                ),
            )
            msg = types.SimpleNamespace(content=None, tool_calls=[tc])
            choice = types.SimpleNamespace(message=msg, finish_reason="tool_calls")
            return types.SimpleNamespace(
                choices=[choice],
                usage=types.SimpleNamespace(prompt_tokens=20, completion_tokens=10),
            )
        msg = types.SimpleNamespace(content="done", tool_calls=None)
        choice = types.SimpleNamespace(message=msg, finish_reason="stop")
        return types.SimpleNamespace(
            choices=[choice],
            usage=types.SimpleNamespace(prompt_tokens=10, completion_tokens=5),
        )

    client.completion = completion  # type: ignore[method-assign]
    return client


def _build_worker(
    tmp_path: Path,
    tool_decisions: dict,
    audit_path: Path,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> AgentWorker:
    """Construct a worker with the audit path redirected into the test dir."""
    # Redirect the audit file to the per-test path so tests are isolated.
    monkeypatch.setenv("KCA_SESSION_ID", "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111")
    monkeypatch.setenv("KCA_AUDIT_PATH", str(audit_path))

    policy = JobPolicy(
        skill_name="_test_fixture",
        policy_profile="permissive-dev",
        mode="default",
        tool_decisions=tool_decisions,
    )
    (tmp_path / "hello.txt").write_text("hello world", encoding="utf-8")
    worker = AgentWorker(
        job_id="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
        prompt="read the file",
        policy=policy,
        workspace=tmp_path,
        db_url=None,
        dry_run=True,
    )
    worker._mock_client = _single_call_client("read_file", {"path": "hello.txt"})
    return worker


def _audit_lines(audit_path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    if not audit_path.is_file():
        return []
    return [json.loads(line) for line in audit_path.read_text().splitlines() if line]


def test_worker_tool_call_allow_path(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    audit = tmp_path / "audit.jsonl"
    worker = _build_worker(
        tmp_path,
        tool_decisions={"read_file": "allow"},
        audit_path=audit,
        monkeypatch=monkeypatch,
    )
    result = worker.run()
    assert result.status == "done", result
    assert result.stop_reason == "end_turn"
    rows = _audit_lines(audit)
    allow_rows = [r for r in rows if r["tool_name"] == "read_file"]
    assert allow_rows, "expected at least one read_file audit row"
    assert allow_rows[-1]["decision"] == "allow"


def test_worker_tool_call_ask_path(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    audit = tmp_path / "audit.jsonl"
    worker = _build_worker(
        tmp_path,
        tool_decisions={"read_file": "ask"},
        audit_path=audit,
        monkeypatch=monkeypatch,
    )
    result = worker.run()
    assert result.status == "paused", result
    assert result.stop_reason == "approval_required"
    rows = _audit_lines(audit)
    ask_rows = [r for r in rows if r["decision"] == "ask"]
    assert ask_rows, "expected an audit row with decision=ask"
    # File should not have been mutated, and the worker should never have hit
    # the "tool_result" path. (Tool ran but produced no side effect for read.)


def test_worker_tool_call_deny_path(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    audit = tmp_path / "audit.jsonl"
    worker = _build_worker(
        tmp_path,
        tool_decisions={"read_file": "deny"},
        audit_path=audit,
        monkeypatch=monkeypatch,
    )
    result = worker.run()
    assert result.status == "failed", result
    assert result.stop_reason == "policy_violation"
    rows = _audit_lines(audit)
    deny_rows = [r for r in rows if r["decision"] == "deny"]
    assert deny_rows, "expected an audit row with decision=deny"
```

```python
"""M9 smoke tests — regression assertions for Spaceship Titanic.

This module is **assertion-only**. It does not retrain models, does not
re-submit to Kaggle, and does not write to the DB. It reads the metrics
recorded by:

  - M9-T002 (baseline LR, ``experiment_runs.external_run_id='baseline-lr'``)
  - M9-T005 (HGB + feature engineering, ``external_run_id='hgb-fe-v1'``)
  - M9-T004 (the single approved real Kaggle submission, recorded in
    ``submissions.public_score``; the submissions row's
    ``experiment_run_id`` FK points back to the baseline-lr run)

and asserts:

  - ``cv_lr >= 0.78``         (M9 sanity guard, see docs/milestones.md §M9)
  - ``cv_hgb >= 0.80``        (M9 sanity guard)
  - ``cv_hgb > cv_lr``        (HGB beat LR on the same CV split)
  - ``public_score IS NOT NULL`` for the M9-T004 submission row

Tests are DB-aware and SKIP cleanly when ``SUPABASE_DB_URL`` is unset, so
the no-DB CI job stays green. The live-DB CI job runs them.

Run with:
    python -m pytest tests/test_m9_smoke.py -v
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT / "tools" / "kca"))

requires_db = pytest.mark.skipif(
    not os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_URL"),
    reason="SUPABASE_DB_URL not set",
)

# M9 thresholds — these are sanity guards copied from docs/milestones.md §M9.
# They are deliberately well below the recorded values so a real regression
# (data leakage, broken CV split, mis-recorded metric) trips them, but
# routine variance from seed/version drift does not.
LR_CV_FLOOR = 0.78
HGB_CV_FLOOR = 0.80

# External run names (experiment_runs.external_run_id).
LR_RUN_NAME = "baseline-lr"
HGB_RUN_NAME = "hgb-fe-v1"

# The one real Kaggle submission from M9-T004, identified by its
# Kaggle-side submission id. Looking up by external_submission_id keeps
# the test stable across DB recreations.
M9_T004_EXTERNAL_SUBMISSION_ID = "52955657"


def _fetch_cv_accuracy(cur, external_run_id: str) -> float:
    """Return the recorded cv_accuracy for an experiment_runs row.

    Reads ``metrics->'cv_accuracy'->>'value'`` which is the shape
    written by the M2 metrics path (see ``tools/kca/db.py::record_metric``).
    """
    cur.execute(
        """
        SELECT (metrics->'cv_accuracy'->>'value')::float AS cv_accuracy
        FROM experiment_runs
        WHERE external_run_id = %s
        ORDER BY created_at DESC
        LIMIT 1
        """,
        (external_run_id,),
    )
    row = cur.fetchone()
    assert row is not None, (
        f"no experiment_runs row with external_run_id={external_run_id!r}"
    )
    cv = row[0]
    assert cv is not None, (
        f"experiment_runs[{external_run_id!r}].metrics->'cv_accuracy'->>'value' is NULL"
    )
    return float(cv)


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def m9_metrics():
    """Read all four M9 regression metrics from the DB in one connection."""
    import psycopg

    with psycopg.connect(os.environ["SUPABASE_DB_URL"]) as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cv_lr = _fetch_cv_accuracy(cur, LR_RUN_NAME)
            cv_hgb = _fetch_cv_accuracy(cur, HGB_RUN_NAME)

            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT id, public_score, experiment_run_id
                FROM submissions
                WHERE external_submission_id = %s
                """,
                (M9_T004_EXTERNAL_SUBMISSION_ID,),
            )
            sub = cur.fetchone()

    assert sub is not None, (
        f"no submissions row with external_submission_id={M9_T004_EXTERNAL_SUBMISSION_ID!r}; "
        "M9-T004 LB record is missing"
    )
    return {
        "cv_lr": cv_lr,
        "cv_hgb": cv_hgb,
        "submission_id": sub[0],
        "public_score": sub[1],
        "submission_experiment_run_id": sub[2],
    }


@requires_db
def test_lr_cv_meets_floor(m9_metrics):
    cv = m9_metrics["cv_lr"]
    assert cv >= LR_CV_FLOOR, (
        f"LR baseline cv_accuracy={cv:.6f} fell below M9 floor {LR_CV_FLOOR}; "
        "do NOT lower the threshold — investigate the run first"
    )


@requires_db
def test_hgb_cv_meets_floor(m9_metrics):
    cv = m9_metrics["cv_hgb"]
    assert cv >= HGB_CV_FLOOR, (
        f"HGB+FE cv_accuracy={cv:.6f} fell below M9 floor {HGB_CV_FLOOR}; "
        "do NOT lower the threshold — investigate the run first"
    )


@requires_db
def test_hgb_beats_lr_on_cv(m9_metrics):
    cv_lr = m9_metrics["cv_lr"]
    cv_hgb = m9_metrics["cv_hgb"]
    assert cv_hgb > cv_lr, (
        f"HGB CV {cv_hgb:.6f} did NOT beat LR CV {cv_lr:.6f}; "
        "the second experiment is expected to improve over the baseline"
    )


@requires_db
def test_m9_t004_public_score_recorded(m9_metrics):
    score = m9_metrics["public_score"]
    assert score is not None, (
        f"submissions row for external_submission_id="
        f"{M9_T004_EXTERNAL_SUBMISSION_ID!r} has NULL public_score"
    )
    # Sanity: a Kaggle accuracy LB score sits in (0, 1].
    assert 0.0 < float(score) <= 1.0, (
        f"public_score={score!r} outside plausible range (0, 1]"
    )
```

```python
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as _dt
import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import time
from pathlib import Path

from _types import EXIT_OK, EXIT_BLOCKED, EXIT_RUNTIME, SideEffect
from _util import warn

import db

_GATE_ENV = "KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE"


# ADR-0006 default policy: True = require approval, False = allow.
OPERATION_DEFAULTS = {
    "kaggle_submit": False,
    "kernel_push": False,
    "dataset_upload": True,
    "git_push": False,
    "git_force_push": True,
    "supabase_migrate": True,
    "delete_artifact": True,
    "external_fetch": False,
}


class ApprovalRequired(Exception):
    """Raised when a gated operation lacks approval under the active policy."""

    def __init__(self, operation: str, policy: dict):
        self.operation = operation
        self.policy = policy
        super().__init__(f"ApprovalRequired: {operation}")


def _check_approval_gate(operation: str, policy: dict) -> None:
    """Raise ApprovalRequired if `policy` (or defaults) gates `operation`.

    KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1 remains an emergency CI override.
    """
    gates = (policy or {}).get("approval_gates", {})
    requires = gates.get(operation, OPERATION_DEFAULTS.get(operation, True))
    if requires and not os.environ.get(_GATE_ENV):
        raise ApprovalRequired(operation, policy or {})


def _gate(side_effect: SideEffect, command_name: str) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
    if side_effect in (SideEffect.READ_ONLY, SideEffect.LOCAL_WRITE):
        return True, None
    if os.environ.get(_GATE_ENV) == "1":
        warn(f"REMOTE OPERATION: kaggle {command_name} — {_GATE_ENV} is set")
        return True, None
    return False, f"remote operation requires {_GATE_ENV}=1 and human approval"


def _record_approval(command_name: str, options: dict) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    """Insert a pending human_decisions row. Returns (approval_id, warning).

    Best-effort: DB failures never block the refusal path. Caller emits the
    blocked envelope regardless.
    """
    args_summary = ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in options.items() if v is not None)
    prompt = f"Approve Kaggle {command_name} ({args_summary or 'no args'})"
    try:
        approval_id = db.insert_approval_request(
            decision_type=f"kaggle.{command_name}",
            prompt=prompt,
            options=options,
        )
        return approval_id, None
    except Exception as e:
        return None, f"approval recording failed: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"


def _emit_blocked(
    command_name: str,
    side_effect: SideEffect,
    reason: str,
    options: dict | None = None,
) -> int:
    payload = {
        "ok": False,
        "error": reason,
        "command": f"kaggle {command_name}",
        "side_effect": side_effect.value,
    }
    # Best-effort: record the attempt in human_decisions.
    if options is not None:
        approval_id, warning = _record_approval(command_name, options)
        if approval_id:
            payload["approval_request_id"] = approval_id
            payload["approval_recorded"] = True
        else:
            payload["approval_recorded"] = False
            if warning:
                payload["approval_warning"] = warning
                warn(warning)
    print(json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False))
    return EXIT_BLOCKED


def _emit_stub(
    command_name: str, side_effect: SideEffect, extra: dict | None = None
) -> int:
    out = {
        "ok": True,
        "stub": True,
        "command": f"kaggle {command_name}",
        "side_effect": side_effect.value,
    }
    if extra:
        out.update(extra)
    print(json.dumps(out, ensure_ascii=False))
    return EXIT_OK


def _emit_json(payload: dict) -> int:
    print(json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False))
    return EXIT_OK if payload.get("ok") else EXIT_RUNTIME


def _policy_from_env() -> dict:
    """Load a JSON policy blob from KCA_POLICY env if present; else empty."""
    raw = os.environ.get("KCA_POLICY")
    if not raw:
        return {}
    try:
        return json.loads(raw)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return {}


def cmd_submit(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    se = SideEffect.SUBMISSION
    competition = args.competition
    file_path = args.file
    message = args.message or "kca agent submission"

    if not os.environ.get("KAGGLE_USERNAME"):
        return _emit_json(
            {
                "ok": False,
                "error": "KAGGLE_USERNAME not set; cannot submit",
                "competition": competition,
                "side_effect": se.value,
            }
        )
    if not os.environ.get("KAGGLE_KEY"):
        return _emit_json(
            {
                "ok": False,
                "error": "KAGGLE_KEY not set; cannot submit",
                "competition": competition,
                "side_effect": se.value,
            }
        )

    try:
        _check_approval_gate("kaggle_submit", _policy_from_env())
    except ApprovalRequired:
        return _emit_blocked(
            "submit",
            se,
            "ApprovalRequired: kaggle_submit",
            options={"competition": competition, "file": file_path, "message": message},
        )

    proc = subprocess.run(
        [
            "kaggle",
            "competitions",
            "submit",
            "-c",
            competition,
            "-f",
            file_path,
            "-m",
            message,
        ],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    return _emit_json(
        {
            "ok": proc.returncode == 0,
            "competition": competition,
            "file": file_path,
            "side_effect": se.value,
            "stdout": proc.stdout,
            "stderr": proc.stderr,
        }
    )
```

```python
"""kca decisions: list, approve, and deny human approval requests."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json

from _types import EXIT_OK, EXIT_RUNTIME, SideEffect


def _emit(ok: bool, payload: dict, exit_code: int = EXIT_OK) -> int:
    print(json.dumps({"ok": ok, **payload}, ensure_ascii=False))
    return exit_code


def _load_db():
    """Import db module; raise ImportError or DBNotConfigured if unavailable."""
    import db as _db

    return _db


def cmd_list(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    try:
        _db = _load_db()
        job_id = getattr(args, "job_id", None)
        rows = _db.list_pending_decisions(job_id=job_id)
        decisions = [
            {
                "id": str(r.get("id", "")),
                "decision_type": r.get("decision_type", ""),
                "status": r.get("status", ""),
                "prompt": r.get("prompt", ""),
                "created_at": str(r.get("created_at", "")),
                "job_id": str(r.get("job_id", "")) if r.get("job_id") else None,
            }
            for r in rows
        ]
        payload: dict = {
            "decisions": decisions,
            "side_effect": SideEffect.READ_ONLY.value,
        }
        if getattr(args, "include_reviews", False):
            review_rows = _db.list_reviews(job_id=job_id, limit=50)
            payload["reviews"] = [
                {
                    "id": str(r.get("id", "")),
                    "job_id": str(r.get("job_id", "")) if r.get("job_id") else None,
                    "verdict": r.get("verdict", ""),
                    "target_op": r.get("target_op", ""),
                    "reviewer_model": r.get("reviewer_model", ""),
                    "rationale": (r.get("rationale") or "")[:200],
                    "created_at": str(r.get("created_at", "")),
                }
                for r in review_rows
            ]
        return _emit(True, payload)
    except Exception as exc:
        # Exit 0 with ok=false for graceful DB-unavailable degradation.
        return _emit(False, {"error": str(exc), "decisions": []})


def cmd_approve(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    try:
        _db = _load_db()
        notes = getattr(args, "notes", None)
        _db.resolve_decision(args.id, "approved", notes=notes)
        # If the decision is linked to a job, append an approval_resume event
        # so a subsequent `scripts/run_job.py --job-id <uuid>` resume path can
        # find it.
        job_id = None
        try:
            row = _db.get_decision(args.id)
            job_id = row.get("job_id")
        except Exception:
            job_id = None
        if job_id:
            try:
                _db.append_job_event(
                    str(job_id),
                    "approval_resume",
                    event_data={"decision_id": args.id},
                )
            except Exception:
                pass
        return _emit(
            True,
            {
                "decision_id": args.id,
                "resolution": "approved",
                "job_id": str(job_id) if job_id else None,
                "side_effect": SideEffect.LOCAL_WRITE.value,
            },
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        return _emit(False, {"error": str(exc)}, EXIT_RUNTIME)


def cmd_deny(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    try:
        _db = _load_db()
        notes = getattr(args, "notes", None)
        _db.resolve_decision(args.id, "rejected", notes=notes)
        return _emit(
            True,
            {
                "decision_id": args.id,
                "resolution": "rejected",
                "side_effect": SideEffect.LOCAL_WRITE.value,
            },
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        return _emit(False, {"error": str(exc)}, EXIT_RUNTIME)


def add_parsers(sub: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    dec = sub.add_parser("decisions", help="Manage pending human approval decisions")
    dec_sub = dec.add_subparsers(dest="decisions_cmd", required=True)

    p_list = dec_sub.add_parser("list", help="List pending decisions (READ_ONLY)")
    p_list.add_argument(
        "--pending",
        action="store_true",
        help="Filter to pending status only (default behaviour)",
    )
    p_list.add_argument(
        "--job-id", dest="job_id", default=None, help="Filter to a specific job"
    )
    p_list.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=20)
    p_list.add_argument(
        "--include-reviews",
        dest="include_reviews",
        action="store_true",
        help="Also surface reviewer verdict rows (M6)",
    )
    p_list.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_list.set_defaults(func=cmd_list)

    p_approve = dec_sub.add_parser(
        "approve", help="Approve a pending decision (LOCAL_WRITE)"
    )
    p_approve.add_argument("--id", required=True, help="decision_id to approve")
    p_approve.add_argument("--notes", default=None)
    p_approve.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_approve.set_defaults(func=cmd_approve)

    p_deny = dec_sub.add_parser("deny", help="Deny a pending decision (LOCAL_WRITE)")
    p_deny.add_argument("--id", required=True, help="decision_id to deny")
    p_deny.add_argument("--notes", default=None)
    p_deny.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_deny.set_defaults(func=cmd_deny)
```

```python
from __future__ import annotations

import json

from pathlib import Path

def _env_clean(**overrides) -> dict:
    """Copy os.environ minus DB/Kaggle/API keys; apply overrides last."""
    env = os.environ.copy()
    for k in (
        "SUPABASE_DB_URL",
        "KCA_DB_TARGET",
        "KAGGLE_USERNAME",
        "KAGGLE_KEY",
        "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY",
        "KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE",
    ):
        env.pop(k, None)
    for k, v in overrides.items():
        if v is None:
            env.pop(k, None)
        else:
            env[k] = v
    return env


def _run(argv, cwd=None, env=None) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return subprocess.run(
        argv,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=False,
        env=env if env is not None else _env_clean(),
        cwd=str(cwd) if cwd is not None else str(REPO_ROOT),
    )
```

```python
"""M1 smoke tests for the kca CLI.

Each test invokes kca via subprocess so the CLI surface is what's exercised,
not the internals. No network. Uses tmp_path for filesystem isolation.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
KCA = [sys.executable, str(REPO_ROOT / "tools" / "kca" / "kca.py")]

# As of M2-T004, `kca run` is DB-first. Tests that exercise it skip when no DB
# is configured. Set KCA_DB_TARGET=local + SUPABASE_DB_URL to enable them.
requires_db = pytest.mark.skipif(
    not (os.environ.get("KCA_DB_TARGET") and os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_URL")),
    reason="kca run tests need KCA_DB_TARGET=local + SUPABASE_DB_URL (M2-T004 DB-first).",
)


def _run(
    *argv: str, env: dict | None = None, cwd: Path | None = None
) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    full_env = os.environ.copy()
    if env is not None:
        for k, v in env.items():
            if v is None:
                full_env.pop(k, None)
            else:
                full_env[k] = v
    return subprocess.run(
        [*KCA, *argv],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=False,
        env=full_env,
        cwd=str(cwd or REPO_ROOT),

def _parse_json(proc: subprocess.CompletedProcess) -> dict:
    stdout = (proc.stdout or "").strip()
    assert stdout, f"empty stdout; stderr={proc.stderr!r}"
    return json.loads(stdout)

    payload = _parse_json(proc)
    assert payload["ok"] is True
    assert payload["side_effect"] == "LOCAL_WRITE"
    assert dst.exists()
```

```python
class MockLiteLLMClient:
    """Deterministic LiteLLM mock. Never calls any real API."""

    def __init__(self, scenario: str = "two_turns"):
        self._turn = 0
        self._scenario = scenario

    def completion(self, **kwargs) -> object:
        self._turn += 1
        if self._scenario == "two_turns":
            if self._turn == 1:
                return _make_tool_calls_response(
                    "read_file", {"path": "README.md"}, 50, 20
                )
            return _make_stop_response("dry run complete", 30, 10)
        if self._scenario == "infinite_tool":
            return _make_tool_calls_response(
                "read_file", {"path": "README.md"}, 100, 50
            )
        raise ValueError(f"unknown scenario: {self._scenario}")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# AgentWorker
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class AgentWorker:
    """Competition agent worker using LiteLLM as the provider layer (ADR-0004)."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        job_id: str,
        prompt: str,
        policy: JobPolicy,
        workspace: Path,
        db_url: str | None = None,
        model: str | None = None,
        dry_run: bool = False,
        resume_state: dict | None = None,
    ):
        self.job_id = job_id
        self.prompt = prompt
        self.policy = policy
        self.workspace = Path(workspace)
        self.db_url = db_url
        self.dry_run = dry_run
        # Optional resume state: {turns_used, cost_usd, last_msg, allow_once}
        self.resume_state = resume_state or {}
        # model kwarg overrides policy.model when given
        if model is not None:
            self.policy = JobPolicy(
                max_turns=policy.max_turns,
                max_cost_usd=policy.max_cost_usd,
                max_runtime_s=policy.max_runtime_s,
                allowed_tool_patterns=policy.allowed_tool_patterns,
                model=model,
                temperature=policy.temperature,
                top_p=policy.top_p,
                min_p=policy.min_p,
                approval_gates=policy.approval_gates,
                max_side_effect=policy.max_side_effect,
                skill_name=getattr(policy, "skill_name", None),
                policy_profile=getattr(policy, "policy_profile", "default"),
                mode=getattr(policy, "mode", "default"),
                tool_decisions=dict(getattr(policy, "tool_decisions", {})),
            )
        # Allow test code to override the mock scenario or inject a client directly.
        self._mock_scenario: str = "two_turns"
        self._mock_client: MockLiteLLMClient | None = None

    def run(self) -> WorkerResult:
        from src.worker import telemetry as _otel

        # Only tag spans with a job_id when we know that row exists in the DB
        # (otherwise the Supabase exporter trips on the agent_jobs FK).
        tracer_job_id = self.job_id if self.db_url else None
        tracer = _otel.build_tracer(job_id=tracer_job_id)
        if tracer.is_enabled():
            job_span = _otel.start_job_span(tracer, self.job_id, self.prompt)
            try:
                if self.db_url and self.job_id:
                    self._safe_set_job_trace(tracer.trace_id, job_span.span_id)
            except Exception:
                pass
        else:
            job_span = None
        try:
            return self._run_inner(tracer)
        finally:
            if job_span is not None:
                job_span.end()

    def _safe_set_job_trace(self, trace_id: str, root_span_id: str) -> None:
        try:
            import sys as _sys

            _sys.path.insert(
                0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "tools" / "kca")
            )
            import db as _db

            _db.set_job_trace(self.job_id, trace_id, root_span_id)
        except Exception:
            pass

    def _run_inner(self, tracer) -> WorkerResult:
        from src.worker import telemetry as _otel

        if self._mock_client is not None:
            client = self._mock_client
        elif self.dry_run:
            client = MockLiteLLMClient(scenario=self._mock_scenario)
        else:
            client = None
        budget = BudgetTracker(self.policy, model=self.policy.model)
        # Seed from resume_state so cumulative turns/cost roll forward.
        if self.resume_state:
            budget.turns = int(self.resume_state.get("turns_used") or 0)
            budget.cost_usd = float(self.resume_state.get("cost_usd") or 0.0)
        executor = ToolExecutor(self.workspace, self.policy)
        # One-shot allowlist for the paused tool_input from a prior pause.
        allow_once = (self.resume_state or {}).get("allow_once") or None
        messages: list[dict] = [{"role": "user", "content": self.prompt}]
        start = time.monotonic()

        while True:
            # 1. Pre-turn budget check
            stop_reason = budget.check_limits()
            if stop_reason:
                self._update_status("failed", error=stop_reason, budget=budget)
                return WorkerResult(
                    status="budget_stop",
                    turns_used=budget.turns,
                    cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
                    duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
                    final_message="",
                    stop_reason=stop_reason,
                )

            # 2. LiteLLM call (OpenAI format for all providers)
            extra: dict = (
                {} if self.policy.min_p is None else {"min_p": self.policy.min_p}
            )
            with _otel.with_turn_span(tracer, budget.turns + 1) as _turn_span:
                if client is not None:
                    response = client.completion(
                        model=self.policy.model,
                        max_tokens=8192,
                        tools=TOOL_SCHEMAS,
                        messages=messages,
                        temperature=self.policy.temperature,
                        top_p=self.policy.top_p,
                        **extra,
                    )
                else:
                    import litellm

                    response = litellm.completion(
                        model=self.policy.model,
                        max_tokens=8192,
                        tools=TOOL_SCHEMAS,
                        messages=messages,
                        temperature=self.policy.temperature,
                        top_p=self.policy.top_p,
                        **extra,
                    )
                if _turn_span is not None:
                    _turn_span.set_attribute("model", self.policy.model)
                    usage = getattr(response, "usage", None)
                    if usage is not None:
                        _turn_span.set_attribute(
                            "prompt_tokens",
                            getattr(usage, "prompt_tokens", 0),
                        )
                        _turn_span.set_attribute(
                            "completion_tokens",
                            getattr(usage, "completion_tokens", 0),
                        )

            # 3. Record turn cost
            budget.record_turn(response)
            msg = response.choices[0].message
            finish_reason = response.choices[0].finish_reason

            self._append_event(
                "turn_start",
                budget.turns,
                input_tokens=getattr(response.usage, "prompt_tokens", 0),
                output_tokens=getattr(response.usage, "completion_tokens", 0),
                cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
                event_data={"finish_reason": finish_reason},
            )

            # 4. stop → job done
            if finish_reason == "stop":
                final_text = msg.content or ""
                self._update_status("succeeded", budget=budget)
                return WorkerResult(
                    status="done",
                    turns_used=budget.turns,
                    cost_usd=budget.cost_usd,
                    duration_s=time.monotonic() - start,
                    final_message=final_text,
                    stop_reason="end_turn",
                )

            # 5. tool_calls → execute each tool
            if finish_reason == "tool_calls":
                tool_calls = msg.tool_calls or []
                # Append assistant turn with tool_calls (OpenAI message format)
                messages.append(
                    {
                        "role": "assistant",
                        "content": msg.content,
                        "tool_calls": [
                            {
                                "id": tc.id,
                                "type": "function",
                                "function": {
                                    "name": tc.function.name,
                                    "arguments": tc.function.arguments,
                                },
                            }
                            for tc in tool_calls
                        ],
                    }
                )
                for tc in tool_calls:
                    tool_input = json.loads(tc.function.arguments)
```

```python
"""M9-T002 baseline logistic-regression experiment for Spaceship Titanic.

Trains a single LR baseline with a small, deterministic preprocessing
pipeline and reports a stratified k-fold CV accuracy. Writes a Kaggle
``submission.csv`` for the test set into the run artifact directory.

This script is intentionally minimal and reproducible:

  * seed = 42, folds = 5 (StratifiedKFold).
  * Features: existing numeric columns + Cabin-derived deck/side, plus
    one-hot encoded low-cardinality categoricals. Names and PassengerId
    are dropped as identifiers.
  * Model: ``sklearn.linear_model.LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000)``.

Usage::

    python scripts/baseline_lr_spaceship.py \
        --data-dir data/spaceship-titanic \
        --run-dir runs/spaceship-titanic/baseline-lr

Outputs:
  - ``<run-dir>/submission.csv``  (PassengerId, Transported)
  - ``<run-dir>/cv_summary.json`` (per-fold scores, seed, folds)

The CV score should be recorded into the ``runs`` table via
``kca run record-metric --key cv_accuracy --value <score>``; this script
prints the score to stdout for that step.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold, cross_val_score
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder, StandardScaler


SEED = 42
N_FOLDS = 5


def _split_cabin(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cabin is 'Deck/Num/Side'. Split into Deck and Side; drop Num."""
    cabin = df["Cabin"].astype("string")
    parts = cabin.str.split("/", expand=True)
    deck = parts[0].fillna("Missing")
    side = (
        parts[2].fillna("Missing")
        if parts.shape[1] >= 3
        else pd.Series("Missing", index=df.index)
    )
    out = df.copy()
    out["Deck"] = deck.astype("string")
    out["Side"] = side.astype("string")
    return out.drop(columns=["Cabin"])


def _prep(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = _split_cabin(df)
    # Drop identifiers / free-text columns.
    df = df.drop(columns=["Name"], errors="ignore")
    return df


def _build_pipeline(numeric_cols: list[str], categorical_cols: list[str]) -> Pipeline:
    numeric_pipe = Pipeline(
        steps=[
            ("imputer", SimpleImputer(strategy="median")),
            ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
        ]
    )
    categorical_pipe = Pipeline(
        steps=[
            ("imputer", SimpleImputer(strategy="most_frequent")),
            ("ohe", OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore", sparse_output=False)),
        ]
    )
    pre = ColumnTransformer(
        transformers=[
            ("num", numeric_pipe, numeric_cols),
            ("cat", categorical_pipe, categorical_cols),
        ]
    )
    clf = LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000, random_state=SEED)
    return Pipeline(steps=[("pre", pre), ("clf", clf)])


def main() -> int:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--data-dir", default="data/spaceship-titanic")
    p.add_argument("--run-dir", default="runs/spaceship-titanic/baseline-lr")
    args = p.parse_args()

    data_dir = Path(args.data_dir)
    run_dir = Path(args.run_dir)
    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    train = pd.read_csv(data_dir / "train.csv")
    test = pd.read_csv(data_dir / "test.csv")
    sample = pd.read_csv(data_dir / "sample_submission.csv")

    y = train["Transported"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    train_feat = _prep(train.drop(columns=["Transported"]))
    test_feat = _prep(test)

    # Choose columns AFTER prep so Deck/Side are picked up.
    numeric_cols = [
        c
        for c in train_feat.columns
        if train_feat[c].dtype.kind in {"f", "i"} and c != "PassengerId"
    ]
    categorical_cols = [
        c for c in train_feat.columns if c not in numeric_cols and c != "PassengerId"
    ]

    pipe = _build_pipeline(numeric_cols, categorical_cols)

    X_train = train_feat.drop(columns=["PassengerId"])
    X_test = test_feat.drop(columns=["PassengerId"])

    skf = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=N_FOLDS, shuffle=True, random_state=SEED)
    scores = cross_val_score(pipe, X_train, y, cv=skf, scoring="accuracy", n_jobs=1)
    cv_mean = float(np.mean(scores))
    cv_std = float(np.std(scores))

    pipe.fit(X_train, y)
    preds = pipe.predict(X_test)
    preds_bool = preds.astype(bool)

    submission = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "PassengerId": test_feat["PassengerId"].to_numpy(),
            "Transported": preds_bool,
        }
    )
    # Preserve sample_submission ordering for safety.
    sub_path = run_dir / "submission.csv"
    submission = (
        submission.set_index("PassengerId").loc[sample["PassengerId"]].reset_index()
    )
    submission.to_csv(sub_path, index=False)

    summary = {
        "seed": SEED,
        "folds": N_FOLDS,
        "model": "LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000)",
        "cv_metric": "accuracy",
        "cv_scores": [float(s) for s in scores],
        "cv_mean": cv_mean,
        "cv_std": cv_std,
        "n_train": int(len(train)),
        "n_test": int(len(test)),
        "submission_path": str(sub_path),
        "numeric_cols": numeric_cols,
        "categorical_cols": categorical_cols,
    }
    (run_dir / "cv_summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))

    print(json.dumps({"ok": True, **summary}))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```

```python
def _check_token(provided: Optional[str]) -> None:
    expected = os.environ.get(TOKEN_ENV, "")
    if not expected:
        # If the server has no token configured, accept any (local dev only).
        return
    if not provided or not hmac.compare_digest(provided, expected):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="invalid token")


def make_app(
    decisions_module: Optional[object] = None,
    audit_logger: Optional[Callable] = None,
) -> FastAPI:
    """Construct the FastAPI app.

    ``decisions_module`` exposes ``get_decision``, ``resolve_decision``, and
    ``append_job_event``. Tests pass a fake module to avoid touching Supabase.
    """
    app = FastAPI(title="kca decision_api", version="0.1.0")

    def _resolve_db():
        if decisions_module is not None:
            return decisions_module
        import sys
        from pathlib import Path

        sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "tools" / "kca"))
        import db as _db  # type: ignore

        return _db

    def _audit(*, decision: str, decision_id: str, reason: Optional[str]) -> None:
        if audit_logger is not None:
            audit_logger(
                decision=decision, decision_id=decision_id, reason=reason or ""
            )
            return
        try:
            from tools.kca.agent.audit import log_policy_decision  # type: ignore

            log_policy_decision(
                tool="decision_api",
                operation=f"decision_{decision}",
                decision="allow",
                policy_profile="default",
                args={"decision_id": decision_id, "reason_len": len(reason or "")},
            )
        except Exception:
            pass

    def _get_pending(decision_id: str):
        _db = _resolve_db()
        row = _db.get_decision(decision_id)
        if not row:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="not found")
        if row.get("status") != "pending":
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=409,
                detail=f"decision is {row.get('status')}, not pending",
            )
        return row

    @app.post("/decision/{decision_id}/approve")
    def approve(
        decision_id: str,
        body: ApproveBody,
        x_decision_api_token: Optional[str] = Header(default=None),
    ) -> dict:
        _check_token(x_decision_api_token)
        row = _get_pending(decision_id)
        _db = _resolve_db()
        _db.resolve_decision(decision_id, "approved", notes=body.reason)
        _audit(decision="approve", decision_id=decision_id, reason=body.reason)
        return {
            "ok": True,
            "decision_id": decision_id,
            "status": "approved",
            "job_id": row.get("job_id"),
        }

    @app.post("/decision/{decision_id}/reject")
    def reject(
        decision_id: str,
        body: RejectBody,
        x_decision_api_token: Optional[str] = Header(default=None),
    ) -> dict:
        _check_token(x_decision_api_token)
        row = _get_pending(decision_id)
        _db = _resolve_db()
        _db.resolve_decision(decision_id, "rejected", notes=body.reason)
        _audit(decision="reject", decision_id=decision_id, reason=body.reason)
        return {
            "ok": True,
            "decision_id": decision_id,
            "status": "rejected",
            "job_id": row.get("job_id"),
        }

    @app.post("/decision/{decision_id}/ask-improve")
    def ask_improve(
        decision_id: str,
        body: AskImproveBody,
        x_decision_api_token: Optional[str] = Header(default=None),
    ) -> dict:
        _check_token(x_decision_api_token)
        row = _get_pending(decision_id)
        _db = _resolve_db()
        # Append a feedback event so the worker can pick it up on resume.
        if row.get("job_id"):
            _db.append_job_event(
                job_id=str(row["job_id"]),
                event_type="feedback",
                event_data={
                    "feedback": body.feedback,
                    "metric_target": body.metric_target,
                    "source": "decision_api.ask_improve",
                },
            )
        _db.resolve_decision(decision_id, "needs_improvement", notes=body.feedback)
```

```python
"""M9-T007 — end-to-end dry-run smoke test for the Spaceship Titanic loop.

This is the CI-friendly counterpart to ``tests/test_m9_smoke.py`` (the
DB-gated regression-assertion module). It exercises the full M9 path —
research → baseline → CV → ``submission.csv`` → reviewer-gate → decision
approve — *in dry-run mode*, on a tiny fixture slice (~80 train rows / 40
test rows), with **no network**, **no DB**, and **no real Kaggle
credentials**.

Acceptance scope (per docs/tasks/M9-T007-e2e-dryrun-test.md):

  - Run the worker in ``dry_run=True`` mode against a fixture data slice
    and verify the policy + audit wiring fires (audit JSONL row written,
    worker returns ``done``).
  - Produce a valid Kaggle ``submission.csv`` by driving the same
    baseline pipeline used by M9-T002 (``scripts/baseline_lr_spaceship``)
    against the fixture slice with a reduced ``n_splits``.
  - Drive the reviewer-gate decision flow via the decision_api
    ``TestClient`` with an in-memory fake DB (mirrors
    ``tests/test_m8_smoke.py``).
  - Assert that ``tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_submit`` refuses cleanly when
    ``KAGGLE_USERNAME`` / ``KAGGLE_KEY`` are absent — the credentials
    gate must fire before any real Kaggle call could happen.

The whole module SKIPs cleanly if any of the lightweight third-party
imports (``pandas``, ``sklearn``, ``fastapi``) are missing; the test
also does **not** require ``SUPABASE_DB_URL``.

Run with:
    python -m pytest tests/test_m9_e2e.py -v
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import types
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
```
